header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Brooks (Lucent CTO), Miguel Santos (Lucent ML Eng), Priya Nair (Lucent PM)
summary: Discovery and POC scoping for Lucent Robotics. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy), workload sizing and traces, benchmark plan (hosted vs dedicated), integration approach (Node/Python SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured JSON outputs), security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and a proposed 6-week timeline. Agreed next steps: share SOW, collect traces, schedule benchmark runs.
topics: Success criteria; Workload sizing; Benchmarks (hosted vs dedicated); Integration planning (SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, tool/function calling, structured output); Security & compliance; POC timeline
transcript:
00:00 - Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy holidays early, we wanted to kick off the POC scoping for Lucent Robotics. I know we have about 50 minutes. Marcus is here from infra side.
00:35 - Dana Brooks: Thanks Ava, yeah we'll try to be efficient. Quick context: we're building a multi-robot task planner, using LLMs for instruction generation and plan verification. We need low latency for tele-op scenarios, and secure handling of proprietary maps.
01:10 - Marcus Patel: Great. Can you give us the traffic profile? QPS, average prompt length?
01:30 - Miguel Santos: So in production we expect bursts up to ~30 concurrent operator sessions, average 1.5 req/sec per operator, peak 45 QPS. Prompts average 180 tokens in, outputs 120 tokens. Some calls are short (5-20 tokens) for yes/no checks.
02:05 - Ava Chen: Good — that's the sizing we need. For success criteria, teams usually pick latency SLO, throughput target and quality metrics. What are your thresholds?
02:28 - Priya Nair: Latency target: end-to-end under 300ms for the short checks, ideally <200ms for critical tele-op confirmations. For throughput we need sustained 35-40 QPS with headroom for burst. Accuracy: structured JSON output must pass our downstream validator 98% of the time.
03:05 - Marcus Patel: Important note — burstiness means batching may not help the short checks. We'll look at KV caching and prefix caching for repeated prompts.
03:30 - Dana Brooks: Also we need a path for private deployment later. Initially hosted is fine if data residency and encryption are ok, but we may require VPC/on-prem in phase 2.
04:00 - Marcus Patel: Noted. For benchmarks we recommend: run baseline on Redwood hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints, then a dedicated Reserved capacity run with quantized model variant. We'll measure p95 latency, p99 latency, throughput, cost/tokens.
04:42 - Miguel Santos: Can you run the same model config as our baseline (gpt-ish open model) so results are comparable to our internal tests?
05:05 - Ava Chen: Yes, we'll mirror model family and provide the same tokenizer/sequence settings. We'll need your sample traces to replay realistic sequences.
05:28 - Priya Nair: We'll send 5k example calls including the short checks and long planning prompts. ETA EOD Thursday.
05:50 - Marcus Patel: For integration, folks usually use our Node or Python SDKs and call Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints — same endpoints as OpenAI, with minor headers. That makes porting trivial. We also support function/tool calling semantics and structured outputs with schema validation hooks.
06:20 - Dana Brooks: Can you elaborate on structured output? Our downstream stack expects specific JSON keys and sometimes nested objects — we need deterministic outputs.
06:45 - Marcus Patel: Right. Two approaches: 1) Use function-calling to enforce schema; Redwood will return typed function args. 2) Use streaming with a JSON schema post-checker; we also provide a 'strict-json' mode that attempts to repair and annotate when deviations occur. Both options surfaced in the SDKs.
07:30 - Miguel Santos: Function calling — does that map to our existing tool chain? We have an internal service that ingests function-like payloads.
07:50 - Marcus Patel: Yes, function calls come back as structured args, you can wire them to your service. We also support custom tool wrappers in the SDK so you can register local tool handlers for safety checks.
08:20 - Priya Nair: How does streaming interact with function calls? If we start streaming partial tokens, can we still rely on the final JSON?
08:45 - Ava Chen: Streaming is for progressive UX; function calls are returned when the model emits the complete payload. We recommend waiting for the function call event for strict downstream ingestion, but you can show partial streaming for operator visibility.
09:15 - Dana Brooks: Security questions — SOC 2 status, encryption at rest, SAML/SSO, KMS. Also need audit logs for every inference tied to customer IDs.
09:40 - Marcus Patel: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and limited KMS integrations for Dedicated. Audit logs and per-request metadata tracing are available in the Console. SSO and SCIM for user sync is supported. We'll share the security whitepaper.
10:05 - Miguel Santos: For PII and map images, can we redact before sending? We prefer to send tokenized references only.
10:30 - Ava Chen: Yes, redaction is fine; for benchmarking you can send traces with placeholders. If/when you go to Private deployment, you can keep everything in your VPC.
11:00 - Priya Nair: Timeline? We need this decided by mid-Feb to include in Q1 roadmap. What does Redwood recommend for a 6-week POC plan?
11:20 - Marcus Patel: Typical cadence: Week 0 (kickoff + confirm traces), Week 1 (baseline hosted runs), Week 2 (dedicated runs + quantization tests), Week 3 (latency/throughput tuning, batching and KV cache), Week 4 (integration tests and function-calling wiring), Week 5 (end-to-end validation with your validators), Week 6 (final report + decision). We can compress if you need faster.
12:00 - Dana Brooks: That fits. Can you share the SOW and pricing options now? We prefer a committed months price for Dedicated if numbers look good.
12:18 - Ava Chen: We'll send a draft SOW and two pricing options — hosted usage-based and a 3-month reserved Dedicated price.
12:35 - Miguel Santos: Benchmarks — will Redwood provide scripts to run consistent load (k6 or locust)?
12:50 - Marcus Patel: We'll provide a benchmark harness (k6-based) and a spreadsheet for results. We'll also run a Redwood-hosted baseline so you get a controlled comparison.
13:20 - Priya Nair: What about model variants and quantization — do you support int8 or 4-bit runs for dedicated?
13:40 - Marcus Patel: Yes, Dedicated supports multiple quantization profiles. We'll recommend profiles based on the trace token distribution. For the POC we'll test a full-fp16 variant and a 4-bit quantized variant to compare quality and cost.
14:05 - Dana Brooks: Any gotchas around OpenAI-compatible endpoints? We have code that assumes certain error codes and rate limits.
14:30 - Ava Chen: We mimic the OpenAI API surface but add additional headers and some extended error metadata for debugging. Rate limiting is configurable per-customer; we'll share the SDK docs. Minor differences exist around streaming chunk format but we have adapters.
15:00 - Miguel Santos: For the function-calling tie-in, what about tool security — preventing arbitrary code execution?
15:20 - Marcus Patel: Tool wrappers run inside your environment for Private/Dedicated; the SDK's tool handler is a callback so execution stays client-side. For hosted, we have a safe wrapper pattern and recommend always validating tool outputs before executing.
15:50 - Priya Nair: For success metrics we're going to instrument p95/p99 latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and schema pass rate. Anything else?
16:15 - Ava Chen: Also add error rate and fallbacks fired (how often model failed over to smaller variant), and per-route cost breakdown. We'll capture these in the Console during the POC.
16:45 - Dana Brooks: One operational question — our ops team wants to pin model versions during rollouts. Is that supported?
17:00 - Marcus Patel: Yes — you can pin model versions and define rollout policies (canary, A/B). We'll help set up the canary for your critical route.
17:25 - Miguel Santos: For the benchmark runs, we may need the ability to simulate network jitter to reproduce field latency. Can you support that?
17:45 - Marcus Patel: We'll provide the harness and you can inject latency from the client side; if you want server-side simulated jitter we can arrange a controlled environment in Dedicated.
18:10 - Priya Nair: Any legal or procurement blockers we should know about?
18:30 - Ava Chen: We'll include standard terms; if you need enterprise amendments (data residency, indemnity) we can get legal involved. For procurement, we'll include a procurement checklist with the SOW.
18:55 - Dana Brooks: Good. Let's recap next steps quickly.
19:10 - Ava Chen: Recap: Redwood sends SOW + pricing (Ava) by 12/24, Lucent shares traces and sample prompts (Miguel) by 12/24, Marcus will provision benchmark harness and propose 3 test windows by 12/28, Priya to confirm stakeholder list by 1/3, schedule kickoff week of 1/4.
19:40 - Miguel Santos: Sounds good. One last thing — do you have references for similar robotics customers?
19:55 - Ava Chen: We have a couple of customers in robotics-adjacent spaces and can connect you to a reference if useful.
20:10 - Dana Brooks: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll look out for the SOW and traces.
20:20 - Ava Chen: Thanks all, happy holidays, we'll follow up over email.
